title: Preparing Carboxylic Acids: Four Routes
subject: Chemistry
objective: Four ways to make a carboxylic acid: oxidising primary alcohols and aldehydes, oxidising alkylbenzenes, hydrolysing nitriles and esters, and adding a Grignard reagent to dry ice, which adds one carbon (mechanism with curved arrows).

fill.q: Primary alcohols are oxidised to carboxylic acids by acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or ____.
Partial hydrolysis of a nitrile gives an ____.
RMgX + CO₂, then H₃O⁺, gives an acid with ____ carbon more.

tf.q: Oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid changes the number of carbons.
tf.explain: The carbon count stays the same.

tf.q: Propylbenzene gives benzoic acid with hot KMnO₄.
tf.explain: The whole side chain becomes one COOH.

tf.q: Esters give carboxylic acids on hydrolysis.
tf.explain: Acid hydrolysis gives the acid; basic hydrolysis gives its salt.

ar.a: tert-Butylbenzene is not oxidised to benzoic acid by KMnO₄.
ar.r: Its ring-attached carbon carries no H.

mcq.explain: Two carbons + one from CO₂ = propanoic acid.

mcq.q: The species that attacks CO₂ in the Grignard route is:
mcq.explain: The polar C–Mg bond, carbon δ⁻.

num.q: How many carbons does the acid from CH₃Br via the Grignard route have?

short.solution: C₆H₅Br + Mg (dry ether) → C₆H₅MgBr; + CO₂ → C₆H₅COO⁻ ⁺MgBr; + H₃O⁺ → C₆H₅COOH.

match.explain: Each starting material and reagent gives that acid.
